description: The challenge is to create a public-facing web tool to display images of the sky from the SPHEREx mission, making it easy for anyone to quickly see how they change over time. Users will enter the coordinates of a patch of sky (Right Ascension and declination). Your tool will display a series of images of that patch like a little video, making it easy to spot moving objects.
summary: NASA’s SPHEREx mission launched in May 2025, has mapped 100% of the sky every six months across 102 near-infrared spectral bands(0.75"-" 5.0 μ"m)" , capturing over billion objects. This satellite captures a vast amount of data which no scientist or automated pipeline can sift through a billion overlapping sources alone, and raw Multi-Extension FITS archives lock out the public behind complex python workflows. BEYONDSIGHT is a public, mobile ready web application that transforms SPHEREx and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) NEOSSat archives into an interactive “Google Earth for the cosmos”. Featuring continuous multi-wavelength slider (visible to microwave across DSS, 2MASS, SPHEREx, WISE, IRAS, and Planck), a 384x384 multi-epoch blink and difference imaging comparator with yearly proper-motion rings, on-the-fly 102-band spectrophotometry, and Gaia DR3/NEOSSat overlays, BEYONDSIGHT puts cosmic discovery in everyone's hands, turning a billion points of infrared light into an interactive hunt for new worlds.
details:
1. The Problem: The Billion-Object Bottleneck

Look up at the night sky, what our eyes see in visible light is only a tiny fraction of the cosmic story. Cold sub-stellar objects like brown dwarfs and a hypothetical Planet X, emit almost no visible light, hiding in the near infrared, while nearby stars and solar system bodies reveal themselves only by shifting position across observations taken months or years apart.

 

Since May 2025, NASA’s SPHEREx has been mapping the entire sky every six months in 102 near-infrared wavelength bands ( returning spectral images of more than 1 billion objects. While citizen scientist on projects like Backyard Worlds and WiseView have historically discovered most known brown dwarfs and comets by blinking multi-epoch images, SPHEREx and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) NEOSSat datasets currently face three critical barriers:

·High Technical Friction: Accessing SPHEREx Multi-Extension FITS (MEF) cubes at IRSA or NEOSSat observations at the Canadian Astronomy Data Centre (CADC) requires setting up a Python 3.9+ environment, installing multiple libraries and writing custom code which locks out scientists, students and amateur astronomers.

·Overlapping Sources & Detector Artifacts: Without intuitive difference imaging, contamination bitmask flag, and multi-catalogue overlays, researchers lose hours chasing cosmic rays, detector persistence, hot pixels, fast-moving satellite/debris streaks.

·Wasted Flagship Observatory Time & Orbital Risk: Delays in identifying moving transients or confirming exoplanet transit periods waste priceless follow-up observation hours on JWST, TESS, and ESA’s Ariel, while slow visual tracking of Near-Earth Objects (NEOs) and High Earth Orbit space debris puts active satellites at risk.

 

2. What BEYONDSIGHT Does: Our Solution

It is a zero-install, browser-based astronomical discovery platform that combines 3D/2D all-sky navigation with a multi-epoch cutout comparator and spectral analyser:

·Wavelength Slider:

·Watch objects move over time:

·Subtract & Stack Images to Make Faint Targets Pop:

·102-color Infrared “Fingerprints”

·1-Click Challenge Targets & Shareable Links

 

3. Key Scientific & Technical Innovations

·Multi-Wavelength Sky Exploration- BEYONDSIGHT combines observations from different space telescopes into one interactive platform. Using the wavelength slider on the bottom, user can the universe beyond the visible light, revealing hidden objects, cosmic dust, and celestial structures

·Motion Detection Through Image Comparison

·Advanced Astronomical

·Case Study 1: Barnard’s Star

· Case Study 2: WISE 0855

· Case Study 3: RW Aurigae & R Draconis

 

5. Future of BEYONDSIGHT:

·Education- make astronomy and electromagnetic wavelengths easier to understand through interactive exploration.

·Citizen Science- help enthusiasts examine changing objects and identify interesting candidates for further investigation.

·Future Expansion- integrating more astronomical surveys, additional wavelength ranges and richer time comparisons.
